tape_context.note: Concentrated AI-infrastructure unwind, not a broad risk-off. NVDA premarket 156.49 vs Nov-11 close 173.85 = -9.99% on the open board-level investigation into CEO Jensen Huang. Broad index premarket far milder: QQQ 681.72 vs 690.40 = -1.26%, SPY 755.12 vs 759.80 = -0.62%.
tape_context.data_caveat: Alpaca snapshot prevDailyBar lagged one session (returned Nov-10 closes) at scan time. All gap math in this file is re-based on verified Nov-11 1Day closes: NVDA 173.85, NBIS 154.90, CRWV 60.80, LUNR 12.19, BMNR 19.245.

gappers.catalyst: Reported a large Q3 2026 beat before the open - revenue $980.8M, up 571% YoY, with first positive operating income - and sold off anyway as the whole AI-infrastructure complex de-rated alongside NVDA -10%.
gappers.catalyst_detail: Nebius released Q3 2026 results before market open: revenue $980.8M, up 571% YoY and ahead of the roughly $937M consensus; operating income of +$50.4M against a $130.2M loss a year ago; adjusted EBITDA of $465.8M versus a $5.2M loss; net loss from continuing operations narrowed to $37.5M, or $0.13 per diluted share. Nine-month revenue was $1,962.1M, up 549%. Operating cash outflow from continuing operations was $273.0M for the quarter. The print is a clear beat on every headline line, and the stock is still gapping down about 18%. The company had already run +15.4% on Wednesday in sympathy with CoreWeave's Q3, so today's gap unwinds that entire move and then some, taking NBIS below its Nov-10 close of $133.96.
gappers.why: The beat is being swamped by a sector-wide de-rating rather than contradicted by it. The marginal driver is NVDA, down 9.99% premarket on the open board-level investigation into CEO Jensen Huang, which re-prices every levered AI-capex proxy at once. Against that, the one soft spot in the print gets all the attention: $273M of quarterly operating cash outflow set against a 2026 capex program reported around $19.3B, funded by a $2B Nvidia investment, $4.33B of convertible bonds and Meta prepayments. Financing, not demand, is the bear case for the neoclouds, and a governance shock at their main supplier is exactly the headline that reopens it.
gappers.impact: Reads as a genuine repricing rather than a one-day headline spike, and therefore not something to expect to mean-revert into the open. 41.3M premarket shares is heavy participation. The read-through is complex-wide and visible in today's own list: CRWV -12.9%, BMNR -6.3%, NVDA -10.0%, while QQQ is only -1.3% and SPY -0.6% - this is a concentrated AI-infra unwind, not broad risk-off. The one asymmetry versus peers is that NBIS now has positive operating income and positive adjusted EBITDA, a fundamental floor most neoclouds lack, so it should bottom earlier than the group if the group bottoms.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The gap is sector-flow and governance-headline driven, not a change in the Nebius thesis; the business actually improved this quarter, so there is no durable new information here to hold for weeks.
gappers.opportunity_cost: The book is flat - 0 of 6 position slots used, $100,000 equity all in cash, 0 of 3 weekly trades spent - so nothing existing would be displaced; the real cost is the slot and the correlation budget. Within today's own list it loses to LUNR, which is gapping up on its own fundamentals rather than down on someone else's governance scandal. It also competes directly with CRWV: both are neocloud names, so once either is on, the >0.75 correlation gate makes the second one hard to add, and NBIS is the better of the two on fundamentals. On R:R it fails at the open: a 10% trailing GTC stop sits near $116 and the 3%-minimum rule forbids anything tighter, so roughly $13 of risk needs a ~$154 target to clear 2:1 - that is yesterday's close, back through the entire gap, which is not a credible first objective. No defined support below until the gap fills or the complex stabilizes. Research only; wait for a base.

gappers.catalyst: Q3 2026 beat before the open - revenue $269.35M up 413.6% YoY, GAAP EPS -$0.02, record ~$1.9B backlog and first positive free cash flow - the first estimate beat in roughly five quarters.
gappers.catalyst_detail: Intuitive Machines reported Q3 2026 before the open: revenue of $269.35M, up 413.63% YoY, and GAAP EPS of -$0.02, improved 66.67% YoY. The company reported a record contracted backlog of roughly $1.9B (up from $1.1B earlier in the year) and positive free cash flow, and set a full-year 2026 outlook of $920M revenue with positive adjusted EBITDA, giving no margin or EPS guidance. Market commentary frames this as the first beat after roughly five straight quarters of misses. It follows NASA naming Intuitive Machines to its roughly $10B CLPS 2.0 lunar-services framework earlier this month, and the company carries a $2.79B market cap against a 52-week range of $7.78 to $46.75.
gappers.why: A company the market had priced for perpetual misses delivered a beat, a record backlog and its first positive free cash flow in the same print. That forces a re-rate off a deeply depressed base rather than an incremental move: positive FCF from a pre-profit space name removes the standing dilution-and-cash-burn objection that was the core short case, and the backlog plus CLPS 2.0 gives revenue visibility that the $2.79B cap was not discounting. Short interest had built through a five-month downtrend, so part of today's move is covering into a fundamental catalyst.
gappers.impact: Looks sustainable rather than a one-day spike, with the usual caveat that the first hour of a 14% gap is the worst place to measure. 10.0M premarket shares against a 7.41M average full-day volume is real participation, not a thin print. The backlog and the CLPS 2.0 award are durable, multi-year items, which is what separates this from the rest of today's list. There is no sector read-through to lean on - space names have been pressured by capital rotation into the SpaceX listing, and neither RKLB nor ASTS is gapping with it - so this is idiosyncratic, which is a feature here: it is the only name on today's list not wired to the AI-infra unwind.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: Record backlog, inclusion in the $10B CLPS 2.0 framework and a first positive-FCF quarter are structural changes to the earnings path, not a headline, so this is worth a multi-day or multi-week swing if it holds the gap and clears the Confluence rule on a later /trade check.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Displaces nothing held - the book is flat with $100,000 cash - so the cost is one of three weekly new-trade slots plus the opportunity to deploy that capital elsewhere. Against today's own list it is the best candidate by a wide margin: it is the only name gapping up on its own fundamentals, and it passes the correlation gate trivially because it is uncorrelated with the AI-infra cluster that makes NBIS and CRWV effectively one bet. The honest R:R constraint is entry price, not direction: a stop beneath the $12.19 prior close is about 12.3% of risk from $13.88, which needs roughly $17.30 to clear the 2:1 minimum - above the $15 round number traders are watching but far below the $46.75 52-week high, so achievable but not comfortable. That math only works near $13; chasing above about $14.50 breaks 2:1 at any sane stop. Size by ATR(14) via scripts/size.mjs at 1.0% equity risk before any entry - after a 14% gap ATR is inflated, so the rule will return a smaller position than the 20% cap allows. Research only; execution belongs to market-open or /trade.

gappers.catalyst: Giving back Wednesday's +24.7% post-earnings rally as the AI-infra complex unwinds with NVDA -10%; no new company news since the Nov-10 Q3 double beat.
gappers.catalyst_detail: No fresh CoreWeave news today - this is the unwind of its own earnings move. Q3, released after the Nov-10 close, was a double beat: revenue $3.66B up 168% YoY and ahead of estimates, contracted revenue backlog around $132.5B, full-year guidance raised to $13.0-13.3B, and adjusted profitability guided for the first half of 2028. Management also said it would not tap unsecured debt markets at current yields and would lean on customer-backed financing and prepayments, which was the line that calmed neocloud financing fears and lifted the whole group, NBIS included, on Wednesday. The stock closed Nov 11 at $60.80, up from $48.74 pre-earnings, and is now gapping back to roughly $53. The 52-week range is $40.58 to $138.25.
gappers.why: Mechanically the same unwind as NBIS, from the opposite starting point. CRWV was the stock whose print lifted the group; with NVDA down 10% premarket on the Huang investigation, the AI-bubble and financing narratives both reopen, and the group hands the move back. CRWV gives back the most because it is the highest-beta and most debt-scrutinized name in the cohort - the bull case rests specifically on a financing structure that only works while capital markets stay friendly, so a confidence shock at the group's main supplier hits it hardest. Nothing in the business has changed in 48 hours; this is positioning.
gappers.impact: Reads as forced or institutional repositioning rather than retail noise: 165.2M premarket shares against a 56.95M average full-day volume is extraordinary, and that size argues against a clean intraday mean-reversion. Two levels matter. At roughly $53 the stock is still above the $48.74 pre-earnings close, so the post-earnings gain is not yet fully erased - a break of $48.74 would be the signal the earnings move has failed outright. Below that there is no visible support until the low $40s and the $40.58 52-week low. Read-through is the whole complex: NBIS -18%, BMNR -6%, NVDA -10%, against QQQ only -1.3%.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: Nothing fundamental changed between Tuesday's beat and this morning; the move is flow and sentiment, which by definition has no multi-week thesis attached - though short-term here means do not buy the dip, not fade it.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing held to displace, but this is the worst use of a slot on the list. It is the highest-volatility name here and demands the widest stop: a 10% trail from $53.10 sits near $47.80, which is below the $48.74 pre-earnings marker, so the stop is placed exactly where the bear thesis gets confirmed, and clearing 2:1 from there needs roughly $63.70 - above Wednesday's close and through the whole gap. Strictly worse R:R than LUNR at strictly higher risk. It is also correlation-blocked against NBIS under the >0.75 rule: these are one neocloud bet, and of the two NBIS has the better fundamentals, so if an AI-infra entry is ever taken it should not be this one. The genuine competing use of this capital today is LUNR, which offers an uncorrelated fundamental catalyst at a third of the risk per share. Research only.

gappers.catalyst: No company news; an Ethereum-treasury proxy sliding with the combined crypto and AI risk-off. Latest disclosure (Nov 9) showed 6.07M ETH and $14.3B crypto plus cash and marketable securities, down from $16.2B on Oct 12.
gappers.catalyst_detail: No BitMine-specific catalyst surfaced for today, and the company's own recent disclosures are weekly treasury updates rather than events. The latest, dated Nov 9, put holdings at 6.07M ETH with total crypto plus cash and marketable securities of $14.3B; the same series read $14.5B on Nov 2, $15.0B on Oct 26 and $16.2B on Oct 12, so the treasury has shed roughly $1.9B of mark in a month on ETH price alone while the token count barely moved from 6.03M to 6.07M. The company has repurchased 22.9M shares in 2026 at an average $17.48, about $399.6M in total. This is the second consecutive gappers run in which BMNR appears with a null catalyst, and it is the smallest gap on today's list.
gappers.why: BMNR trades as a levered claim on Ethereum, so the equity moves on two things at once: the mark on the treasury and the premium or discount the market pays over that NAV. In a tape where crypto and high-beta AI are both being de-risked in the same session, those compress together, which is why the equity falls faster than the token. There is no information event here - the market is simply remarking a holding company.
gappers.impact: Beta, not information, which is the finding rather than a gap in the research. 31.9M premarket shares is heavy for an $18 stock, but heavy volume on no news is repricing, not a signal, and it carries no edge in either direction - expect it to keep tracking ETH rather than mean-revert on its own. No read-through to anything in the book. The one real level is the $17.48 buyback average sitting just under the current price: a soft floor, since the company has demonstrated it buys around there, but not a support level in the technical sense.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: A crypto-beta drawdown with no catalyst and no durable thesis; the move is a derivative of an asset price rather than a change in the business, and crypto proxies are not in the favored row of the TRADING-STRATEGY.md rotation table.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Displaces nothing held, and has the weakest claim on capital of the four: the smallest gap at -5.9%, barely over the 5% threshold, zero documented catalyst for the second run in a row, and a thesis that reduces to long ETH - which is not a stock thesis and which this strategy has no mandate for. Taking it would burn one of three weekly trades on unlevered crypto beta while LUNR offers a documented fundamental re-rate for the same slot. It cannot be scored against the 2:1 R:R minimum at all, because with no catalyst there is no defined target to measure reward against; a 10% stop near $16.30 would be risk against an unspecified reward. If crypto exposure is wanted it should be a deliberate allocation decision, not a gapper trade. Pass.
